Technical overview

# How 3D pathfinding works in Unreal Engine 5

Unreal Engine's built-in Recast navmesh can only answer one question: where can I stand? This plugin answers the one that flying AI actually needs: where is there empty air? It is a volumetric 3D navigation and pathfinding plugin for UE5 that turns the whole playable volume into a Sparse Voxel Octree, so drones, dragons, spaceships, helicopters, birds and underwater agents path through real 3D space instead of along a floor.
[★★★★★Rated 5.0 out of 5 from3 ratings on Fab↗](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73?tab=reviews)

The problem

## Why Unreal Engine's navmesh can't do 3D pathfinding

Recast, the navigation system that ships with Unreal Engine 5, voxelizes your level and then extracts the **walkable surfaces** from it, and the result is a set of polygons draped over the floor. That is exactly the right representation for a soldier, and completely the wrong one for a dragon. A flying AI has no floor to walk on, so a Recast navmesh gives it nothing to query.

The usual workarounds all leak. Raycast-and-steer looks fine in an open field and gets stuck the moment there is a concave building. Hand-placed waypoint graphs are expensive to author and go stale the instant a level artist moves a wall. Stacking navmeshes at several altitudes turns 3D navigation into a set of disconnected 2D floors, and still can't route diagonally through a shaft.

Volumetric navigation solves it properly by inverting the question. Instead of storing where geometry is, it stores where it isn't, in a Sparse Voxel Octree, and pathfinds through that empty volume in full 3D.

_A bird flock threading rings in mid-air: there is no floor to walk on_

| | UE5 Recast navmesh | LCM 3D Navigation AI (SVO) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it stores | Walkable surfaces: polygons on the floor | Navigable volume: the empty air and water |
| Dimensionality | 2.5D: a surface with height offsets | True 3D: any point in the playable volume |
| Suits | Humanoids, vehicles, ground crowds | Flying AI, drones, spaceships, submarines, insects |
| Vertical movement | Nav links, jumps, stacked meshes | Native: up, down and diagonal are the same query |
| Cost profile | Scales with floor area | Scales with clutter, not level size: open sky is a few large nodes |
| Solvers | A* over polygons | A*, Theta* and Lazy Theta* over octree nodes |
| Crowd scale | Detour crowd manager | 10,000+ agents via Mass Entity, per-agent or shared flow field |
| Can they coexist? | Yes. Run hybrid levels where ground troops use Recast and air units use the SVO. | |

Under the hood

## How volumetric 3D pathfinding works

_The live octree around a sea stack, captured in real time_

01 · The octree

### A Sparse Voxel Octree of the empty space

Drop a single `LcmNavigationManagerSVO` actor into the level and it owns the octree, the pathfinder and every query. The manager subdivides the playable volume only where geometry actually exists: a wide-open sky becomes a handful of large nodes, while a cluttered hangar interior subdivides down to the minimum voxel size. Cost therefore tracks how busy your level is rather than how big it is.

Voxelization, the octree and its links are built on the GPU (D3D12, D3D11 and Vulkan), and each machine's GPU proves its voxels before it builds; one that fails voxelizes on the CPU for that session. Voxels go down to 0.5 cm, so one plugin covers a centimetre-scale aquarium and a streamed open world.

_A hunter's planned route around a container stack_

02 · The solvers

### Three pathfinding solvers, three smoothing modes

Pick the trade-off that fits the agent: **A*** for raw throughput, **Theta*** for true any-angle routes that cut the corners a grid would force you around, and **Lazy Theta*** for near-Theta* path quality at close to A* cost. Solving is multi-threaded and deterministic, so the same input gives the same path every run.

Then choose smoothing (Raw, Linear Shortcut or Curved Spline), each validated against level geometry, so a smoothed path never slices through a wall.

_The world can move underneath them: a drone lands on a moving lorry_

03 · A world that moves

### Dynamic obstacles that restamp, and agents that predict them

Moving geometry writes its own footprint back into the octree as it travels, so lifts, blast doors, destructible cover and patrolling capital ships all change routing live, and in multiplayer that change is multicast to every peer.

Since 3.6, Fly To also predicts each mover's motion and times its pass, so a drone waits for a gate's cycle or slips behind a sweeper instead of re-planning into it.

_A storm cost area: the route bends round it_

04 · Cost areas

### Cost areas priced per agent

Mark volumes as storms, preferred lanes, toll gates or no-fly zones with Unreal's stock NavArea classes. A stock Navigation Query Filter on each agent decides what an area costs that agent, or forbids it, so a cargo drone and a fighter read the same storm differently.

Fly To, Fly To Location, Mass crowds, Find Path and the stock Move To all route by them, across streamed chunk seams too.

The hard part

## Infinite worlds, not a bounded volume

Almost every volumetric navigation implementation for Unreal, including the open-source ones, starts by asking you to place a **bounds volume** and builds its octree inside it.

For an arena or a level-sized map a bounds volume is perfectly fine, and LCM 3D Navigation AI supports exactly that model: a finite world builds once at `BeginPlay` and stays put.

It stops being fine in an open world. A bounds volume has to be big enough to contain everywhere an agent may ever fly, memory scales with that box whether or not anything is happening inside it, and the moment your player crosses the edge, navigation simply ends.

**Infinite mode removes the box.** Navigation chunks stream in around agents and are discarded behind them, so memory stays flat no matter how far the map extends, for the same reason you stream level geometry rather than loading a continent. Long routes use **macro/micro routing**: the path solves coarsely across chunks first and finely within the chunk the agent is actually in, so a cross-map flight never pays full-resolution search cost end to end.

That combination, unbounded streaming navigation with hierarchical routing on top, is what makes 3D pathfinding usable in an open-world or World Partition project rather than only inside a hand-placed box.

**Finite mode**Defined bounds, octree built once at `BeginPlay` or baked to an asset. Lowest overhead when your playable space genuinely is a box.

**Infinite mode**Chunks stream around agents and unload behind, with pre-baked chunks where you want them. Fixed memory budget across an unbounded map.

**Macro / micro routing**Coarse across chunks, fine within them: long routes stay cheap instead of scaling with distance.

A behaviour for every job

## Works with every Unreal Engine AI system

Whichever way your team authors behaviour, the same navigation data is available through every surface, with ready-made behaviours at full parity.

21 tasks, 5 decorators, 5 services

25 tasks, 8 conditions, 8 evaluators

10 tasks, 3 evaluators, on 8 traits

**Fly To Location**One Blueprint node, no AI Controller

**Patrol**Routes between waypoints

**Orbit Target**At a set radius and speed

-

**Follow Target**Formation slots in the leader's frame

**Engage Target**A firing position with line of sight

-

**Scan Area**A volume swept from shared viewpoints

-

**Perch**No two agents on one post

**Land**Onto a moving platform or deck

**Points in SVO Volume**EQS candidates anywhere in 3D

**Reachability 3D**Answered before any search

- **Behaviour Tree**: 21 tasks, 5 decorators and 5 services, including `FlyTo`, Patrol, Orbit Target, Follow Target, Hover, Take Off, Land, Perch, Scan Area, Engage Target, Find Cover, Flee, Investigate, line-of-sight and chunk-loaded checks, with seven documented stock-node patterns showing where an LCM node earns its place over an engine one.

- **StateTree**: 25 tasks, 8 conditions and 8 evaluators at full parity with the Behaviour Tree nodes, so state-driven agents get the same routing and behaviours with no Behaviour Tree in the stack.

- **Mass Entity (ECS)**: eight traits: per-agent asynchronous pathfinding or a shared CPU flow field sampled in O(1) by an entire swarm, driven by auto-registered processors for request, solve and steer. Ten Mass StateTree tasks and three evaluators let crowds perch, scan, engage, investigate and flee. You never call the solver yourself.

- **Blueprint and stock Unreal navigation**: the `Fly To Location` latent node flies any pawn with no Behaviour Tree, StateTree or AI Controller, and Unreal's own Move To, AI Move To and EQS queries plan through the octree.

- **Tactical 3D EQS**: 5 generators, 8 tests and 4 contexts that score real volume: volumetric line-of-sight, cover, threat exposure, height advantage, landing sites and true path distance, so a sniper perch is chosen in 3D rather than on a floor plane.

- **AI Perception and the Gameplay Debugger**: threat tracking, nav links, area modifiers and a live in-editor debugger for inspecting the octree and solved routes, plus a setup wizard and a one-click health check.

Everything is exposed to Blueprint: **726 Blueprint-exposed symbols**, documented in a full API reference, so a complete flying AI can be built without opening Visual Studio. Complete C++ source ships with it when you want it.

Beyond the solver

## Pathfinding is the easy half

A pathfinding plugin hands you a list of points. Turning that into an agent that flies convincingly, is authored by your AI designers, scales to a crowd and survives a multiplayer session is the rest of the work, and in practice it is where the integration time actually goes. That gap is what LCM 3D Navigation AI is built to close.

| Capability | Pathfinding-only plugins | LCM 3D Navigation AI |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route solving | A*, Theta*, Lazy Theta* | The same three solvers |
| World model | Bounds volume required | Finite or infinite streaming chunks |
| Agent locomotion | Bring your own movement | 6-DOF flight & swim component: Multirotor, Jet / Fixed-Wing, Bird, Fish |
| Behaviour Tree | Stock MoveTo nodes | 21 tasks, 5 decorators, 5 services |
| StateTree | Not included | 25 tasks, 8 conditions, 8 evaluators |
| Ready-made behaviours | Not included | Patrol, Orbit, Follow, Hover, Land on moving decks, Perch, Scan Area, Engage, Find Cover, Flee, Investigate |
| Mass Entity crowds | Not included | 8 traits, Mass StateTree behaviours, 10,000+ agents |
| Moving obstacles | Varies | Octree restamping plus Fly To prediction that times its pass |
| Multiplayer | Not included | Server-authoritative replication, deterministic CPU compute |
| Tactical queries | Varies | 3D EQS: 5 generators, 8 tests, 4 contexts scoring real volume |
| Consoles | Varies | PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S |
| Demo content | Varies | 57 demo levels, free from inside the editor |
| Documentation | README | 165-page manual, 15 tutorials, full API reference |
| Support | Community issue tracker | Direct from the developer who wrote it |

Networking

## Server-authoritative multiplayer 3D navigation

Clients request a route, the server solves it and delivers it back through `Client_DeliverPath`, and moving obstacles replay their navigation footprint to every peer over a multicast. CPU compute is bit-deterministic, which keeps replays and lockstep viable, and a headless validation suite (`-LcmMpTest`) exercises the sanity, replicated-request, multicast-transport and digest-chain paths so regressions surface in CI rather than in a playtest.

Supported on **Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S**, with the C++ core held to the same standard on every target; consoles compile from source with your own platform SDK. Dedicated servers and `-nullrhi` runs are supported. Nintendo Switch support is in progress.

Getting started

## Adding 3D pathfinding to a UE5 project

- **Install the plugin**Add LCM 3D Navigation AI from Fab to your Unreal Engine 5.2–5.8 project and enable it in the plugin browser. Open the built-in QuickStart level, or fetch the 57 demo levels from the LCM Nav3D menu › Get the Demo Levels. Installation is chapter 1 of the manual.

- **Place the navigation manager**Drop one `LcmNavigationManagerSVO` into the level and set the world bounds and minimum voxel size. It builds the Sparse Voxel Octree and owns every navigation query from then on.

- **Give the agent a body**Add `LcmFlightMovementComponent` to the pawn and pick an archetype (Multirotor drone, Jet / Fixed-Wing, Bird or Fish), then tune thrust, lift, drag, buoyancy and the attitude PID. An animation-drive struct feeds your blendspaces.

- **Author the behaviour**Use the `FlyTo` Behaviour Tree task, the equivalent StateTree task, a Mass trait for crowds, or the `Fly To Location` Blueprint node for no AI setup at all. Chapter 3 of the manual walks through a first flying agent end to end.

- **Scale up**Add behaviours like Land, Perch, Engage and Flee, dynamic obstacles, cost areas, tactical 3D EQS queries, hybrid Recast levels for ground units, and switch to infinite chunked worlds when the map outgrows a single volume.

Documentation is a **165-page manual with 15 step-by-step tutorials** and a 13-page Quick Start, not a plugin dump: every setting is listed with its verified default and limits, and the full API is documented in a reference. [Read the full documentation online →](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/)

FAQ

## 3D pathfinding in Unreal Engine 5: common questions

### Does Unreal Engine 5 support 3D pathfinding out of the box?

No. UE5 ships with Recast, which builds a navmesh of walkable surfaces: a 2.5D representation designed for characters that stand on the ground. A flying, swimming or space-borne agent has nothing to path along. LCM 3D Navigation AI adds a true volumetric representation that treats open air and water as navigable space, giving Unreal Engine 5 real 3D pathfinding.

### What is the difference between a Recast navmesh and volumetric 3D navigation?

A Recast navmesh describes surfaces you can stand on; it flattens a level into walkable polygons. Volumetric navigation describes the empty space you can move through. LCM 3D Navigation AI carves the playable volume into a Sparse Voxel Octree and paths through the empty nodes, so open sky is stored cheaply as a few large nodes while detail appears only where geometry actually is.

### How do I make flying AI in Unreal Engine 5?

Add an `LcmNavigationManagerSVO` actor so the level can build its navigation octree, give the AI pawn an `LcmFlightMovementComponent` for 6-DOF flight, then drive it from a Behaviour Tree `FlyTo` task, a StateTree task or a Mass Entity trait. For the simplest case, the `Fly To Location` Blueprint node flies a pawn with no AI Controller at all. The plugin handles the request, the solve and the steering; you author the behaviour.

### Does LCM 3D Navigation AI work with Behaviour Trees, StateTree and Mass Entity?

Yes, all three, at full parity and reading the same navigation data. It ships 21 Behaviour Tree tasks, 5 decorators and 5 services; 25 StateTree tasks, 8 conditions and 8 evaluators; and 8 Mass Entity traits with 10 Mass StateTree tasks and 3 evaluators for large crowds. The behaviours include Fly To, Patrol, Orbit, Follow, Hover, Take Off, Land, Perch, Scan Area, Engage Target, Find Cover, Flee and Investigate.

### How many AI agents can it handle?

10,000 or more through Mass Entity. Two crowd modes are available: per-agent asynchronous pathfinding via the Nav3D Agent trait, or a single shared CPU flow field that an entire swarm samples in constant time. Mass StateTree tasks let crowds perch, scan, engage, investigate and flee, and schooling, Hold Avoidance and Contact Push keep dense crowds apart. A per-agent GPU solver is in experimental validation and ships as a free update.

### Does 3D pathfinding work in multiplayer?

Yes, server-authoritatively. Clients request a route, the server solves it and delivers it back through `Client_DeliverPath`, and moving obstacles multicast their navigation footprint. CPU compute stays bit-deterministic for replays and lockstep, and a headless validation suite exercises the replicated paths.

### Does it work in open worlds or with World Partition?

Yes. LCM 3D Navigation AI runs in two modes. A **finite** world builds its octree once at `BeginPlay` inside defined bounds. An **infinite** world has no fixed extent. Navigation chunks stream in around agents and unload behind them, so memory stays flat however far the map runs. Long routes use macro/micro routing, solving coarsely across chunks and finely within the current one. Most volumetric navigation plugins require a bounds volume and cannot navigate outside it. More on infinite worlds →

### How is this different from the free open-source SVO navigation plugins?

The solvers are comparable: A*, Theta* and Lazy Theta* are well established, and the open-source implementations use them too. The difference is everything built around the solver: infinite streaming worlds rather than a required bounds volume, GPU-built navigation, a 6-DOF flight and swim locomotion component, an 85-node Behaviour Tree, StateTree and Mass agent library, moving-obstacle prediction, Mass Entity traits for 10,000+ agent crowds, tactical 3D EQS, server-authoritative multiplayer replication, console support, 57 demo levels, a 165-page manual with 15 tutorials, and direct support from the developer. Compare it product by product →

### How does it compare with Mercuna and other UE5 3D navigation plugins?

Mercuna's cheapest 3D Navigation licence is £2,500 per title (Windows only, no source), against a one-time $199.99 or $1,499.99 for LCM 3D Navigation AI with full C++ source. Fab plugins such as Flying Navigation System cost less but need a bounds volume and have no StateTree or moving-obstacle support, and the free open-source options (AeonixNavigation, Nav3D) need a bounds volume too. None of the alternatives we checked document Mass Entity crowds or a GPU build.

### Is there a 3D navmesh for flying AI in Unreal Engine 5?

Not built in: Unreal's Recast navmesh covers walkable surfaces only. LCM 3D Navigation AI is the volumetric equivalent, a sparse voxel octree of the navigable air and water, built in the editor, at runtime or on the GPU, which flying, swimming and space AI path through the way ground AI uses a navmesh.

### Which Unreal Engine versions and platforms are supported?

LCM 3D Navigation AI 3.6.0 supports Unreal Engine 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7 and 5.8, and is supported on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Consoles compile from source with your own platform SDK. Nintendo Switch support is in progress. Check the [Fab listing](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73) for the current engine compatibility list.

### Do I need C++, or does it work with Blueprints?

It works from Blueprints. The plugin is C++ for performance and ships complete source, but exposes 726 symbols to Blueprint, documented in a full API reference, so a full flying AI can be built without writing code. The `Fly To Location` node flies a pawn from plain Blueprint with no AI Controller. The C++ API is available when you want it.

### Can it handle moving or dynamic obstacles?

Yes. Dynamic obstacles restamp their footprint into the octree as they move, so routes account for doors, lifts, destructible geometry and other moving actors, and the change replicates to clients in multiplayer. Since 3.6, Fly To also predicts every moving obstacle and times its pass: it learns a gate's or a piston's cycle, waits for a gap, takes a detour, and dodges what it cannot outrun.

### Can flying AI land on moving platforms?

Yes. The Land task finds its own landing point and flies the approach relative to the deck, so a drone can land on a rolling ship or a moving lorry and take off again with the deck's velocity. Birds and fish glide in with a braking flare, and EQS generators and tests find landing sites for flying agents.

### Does it work for small worlds such as an aquarium?

Yes. Voxels go down to 0.5 cm, and a World Scale profile handles centimetre-scale worlds. The Fish Tank demo navigates a 120 cm aquarium at 1 cm, with 8 cm fish schooling through a rock arch.

### What is new in LCM 3D Navigation AI 3.6?

Version 3.6.0 (October 2026) adds moving-obstacle prediction to Fly To, the Obstacle Gauntlet demo (a 370 m hall with 42 movers), GPU voxelization that proves itself on each machine before it builds navigation, a self-repairing GPU build on D3D12, D3D11 and Vulkan, more natural fish swimming and schooling, steadier drones and smarter hunters, and more than thirty fixes from a plugin-wide code audit. Full release notes →

### Is there a free demo?

Yes, a free playable demo is on [itch.io](https://uedevlabs.itch.io/lcm-3d-navigation), and buyers get 57 demo levels free from inside the editor (LCM Nav3D menu › Get the Demo Levels). The full plugin is sold on [Fab](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73).

Flying, swimming and free-floating AI, from one hero drone to a 10,000-agent swarm.

**Flying AI and drones**6-DOF flight, landing on moving decks, perching birds and combat drones.

**Underwater and fish AI**Schooling, the whole water column, and aquariums navigated at 1 cm.

**Space combat and dogfights**No floor, no up: chase, intercept and raider swarms in streamed belts.

**Mass Entity crowds**10,000+ agents on paths or a shared flow field, with crowd behaviours.

Flagship UE5 plugin · v3.6.0 · Unreal Engine 5.2–5.8

## Everything in the box

The 3D pathfinding & volumetric navigation plugin for Unreal Engine 5

★ 5.0 on FabSparse Voxel OctreeGPU-built navigation85 AI nodes10,000+ agentsMoving-obstacle predictionMultiplayer replicationBlueprint & C++

**LCM 3D Navigation AI brings true 3D pathfinding to Unreal Engine 5**: flying AI pathfinding for drones, dragons, spaceships, helicopters and underwater agents that Recast navmesh simply cannot express. Unreal's Recast navmesh answers one question: where can I stand? It flattens your level into walkable polygons: exactly right for a soldier, completely wrong for a dragon. LCM 3D Navigation AI answers a different one: where is there empty air? It carves the whole playable volume into a Sparse Voxel Octree and paths through the empty nodes, so open sky costs almost nothing and detail appears only where geometry actually is.

- A* · Theta* · Lazy Theta*: Pathfinding

- GPU build · CPU solve · GPU solver coming soon: Compute

- Finite or Infinite chunks: World mode

- 85 BT · StateTree · Mass: AI nodes

- 01**Sparse Voxel Octree**The level's empty air is subdivided only where geometry exists. One node covers open sky, so cost tracks clutter, not level size. Voxels go down to 0.5 cm, so the same plugin navigates a 120 cm aquarium at 1 cm and a streamed open world. Drop a single `LcmNavigationManagerSVO` per level and it owns the octree, the pathfinder and every query.

- 02**Three solvers, three smoothing modes**A* for raw throughput, Theta* for true any-angle routes, Lazy Theta* for near-Theta* quality at near-A* cost. All three are multi-threaded and deterministic. Then Raw, Linear Shortcut or Curved Spline smoothing, validated against geometry, so a smoothed path never cuts a wall.

- 03**GPU-built navigation that checks itself**Voxelization, the octree and its links are built on the GPU on D3D12, D3D11 and Vulkan. New in 3.6: each machine's GPU proves its voxels before it builds navigation: a capability check, a self-test remembered per GPU and driver, and sampled audits while it runs. A GPU that fails voxelizes on the CPU for that session, and the log says why.

- 04**Macro / micro routing & infinite worlds**Long routes solve coarsely across chunks, then finely within them. Finite worlds build once or bake to an asset; infinite worlds stream chunks around agents and throw them away behind, with pre-baked chunks and a long-range graph that plans beyond loaded geometry.

- 05**Agents that see moving obstacles coming**New in 3.6: Fly To predicts every moving obstacle and times its pass. It learns a gate's or a piston's cycle, turns a spinning blade with it, eases off, waits for a gap or takes a detour, and dodges what it cannot outrun. Moving geometry still restamps the octree, so routes re-plan live.

- 06**A behaviour for every job: 85 AI nodes**Fly To, Patrol, Orbit, Follow, Hover, Take Off, Land (even on a rolling ship's deck), Perch, Scan Area, Engage Target, Find Cover, Flee and Investigate: 31 Behaviour Tree nodes, 41 StateTree nodes and 13 Mass StateTree nodes at full parity. One `Fly To Location` Blueprint node flies any pawn with no AI Controller, and Unreal's own Move To and EQS plan through the octree.

- 07**10,000+ agents through Mass ECS**Eight Mass traits: per-agent asynchronous pathfinding, or one shared CPU flow field sampled O(1) by an entire swarm. Mass StateTree lets crowds perch, scan, engage, investigate and flee; schooling, Hold Avoidance and Contact Push keep dense crowds apart. A per-agent GPU solver is in experimental validation, coming as a free update.

- 08**Tactical EQS in true 3D**5 generators, 8 tests and 4 contexts that score real volume (volumetric line-of-sight, cover, threat exposure, height advantage, landing sites and true path distance), so a sniper perch is chosen in 3D, not on a floor plane.

- 09**6-DOF flight & swim locomotion**Navigation gives guidance; `LcmFlightMovementComponent` turns it into a body. Multirotor drone, Jet / Fixed-Wing, Bird (flap-glide) and Fish (undulatory) archetypes with thrust, lift, drag, buoyancy and attitude PID. Fish hold depth, school in layers and beat their tails with their speed; flight follows the level's gravity.

- 10**Cost areas, priced per agent**Mark volumes as storms, preferred lanes, toll gates or no-fly zones with stock NavArea classes. A stock Navigation Query Filter decides what each area costs each agent, or forbids it, and every planner routes by them, across streamed chunk seams too.

- 11**Server-authoritative multiplayer replication**Clients request a route, the server solves it and delivers it back through `Client_DeliverPath`; moving obstacles replay their nav footprint to every peer over a multicast. A headless validation suite (`-LcmMpTest`) exercises the sanity, replicated-request, multicast-transport and digest-chain paths, and CPU compute stays bit-deterministic for replays and lockstep.

- 12**Built for real projects**Dynamic obstacle restamping, AI Perception threat tracking, hybrid Recast + SVO levels, nav links, area modifiers, a setup wizard, a one-click health check and a live Gameplay Debugger, plus 57 free demo levels you download from inside the editor.

### Works with every Unreal AI system

Whichever way your team authors behaviour, LCM 3D Navigation AI plugs into it: the same navigation data, three authoring surfaces.

Behaviour Tree

21 tasks, 5 decorators and 5 services: `FlyTo`, Patrol, Land, Perch, Engage Target, Find Cover, Flee, Investigate, line-of-sight and chunk-loaded checks, alongside seven documented stock-node patterns showing where an LCM node earns its place.

StateTree

25 tasks, 8 conditions and 8 evaluators at full parity with the Behaviour Tree nodes, so state-driven agents get identical routing and behaviours without a Behaviour Tree in the stack.

Mass Entity

Eight ECS traits (per-agent pathfinding or a shared flow field) plus 10 Mass StateTree tasks and 3 evaluators, so a crowd of 10,000+ entities can perch, scan, engage, investigate and flee.

Plus a **Fly To Location** Blueprint node that flies any pawn with no AI Controller, and Unreal's own Move To, AI Move To and EQS planning through the octree.

Where it differs

## What makes it NextGen

- **Unbounded worlds.** Infinite mode streams navigation chunks around agents and unloads them behind, with pre-baked chunks and a persistent long-range graph, so World Partition and streamed open worlds need no bounds volume.

- **GPU-built navigation that checks itself.** Voxelization, the octree and its links build on the GPU on D3D12, D3D11 and Vulkan; each machine's GPU proves its voxels before it is trusted.

- **Prediction, not just reaction.** Since 3.6, Fly To predicts every moving obstacle and times its pass: it waits for a gap, detours, or dodges what it cannot outrun.

- **One system for every AI author.** 85 ready-made nodes across Behaviour Tree, StateTree and Mass StateTree at full parity, 3D EQS for cover and line of sight, and crowds of 10,000+ agents.

- **Agents that fly and swim.** A 6-DOF movement component with multirotor, jet, bird and fish archetypes turns a route into flight, down to landing on a moving ship's deck.

- **Built to ship.** Server-authoritative multiplayer replication, Unreal Engine 5.2 to 5.8, Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS, PS5 and Xbox, a 165-page manual and 57 free demo levels.

Honest fit

- [**Smart Flying Navigation**](https://www.fab.com/listings/256ea996-5989-4c8c-b9f4-ce2182fe0999)Free on Fab for UE 5.6: an editor-baked octree with A*, Lazy Theta* and ORCA avoidance, Windows only.

- [**3D Path Finding**](https://www.fab.com/listings/f38f8172-7409-4a4c-b7bd-7e166ef75a96)Fab, $99.99 / $349.99, UE 5.0 to 5.8: a 3D grid with Behaviour Tree support; avoidance is in progress.

- [**DoN's 3D Pathfinding (DonAINavigation)**](https://github.com/VSZue/DonAINavigation)Free (MIT), built for UE4: its last substantive update targets UE 4.19 (2018).

FAQ

## Common questions

### What is the best 3D pathfinding plugin for Unreal Engine 5?

It depends on scope. For a complete system (open worlds without a bounds volume, Behaviour Tree, StateTree and Mass Entity crowds, moving-obstacle prediction and multiplayer replication), LCM 3D Navigation AI covers the most ground at a one-time Fab price of $199.99. For a single bounded level on a tight budget, Flying Navigation System ($49.99) is the established Fab option, and AeonixNavigation (beta) and Nav3D are free and open source.

### Is there a cheaper alternative to Mercuna for Unreal Engine 5?

Yes. LCM 3D Navigation AI costs $199.99 (Personal) or $1,499.99 (Professional) as a one-time Fab purchase with full C++ source. Mercuna's cheapest 3D Navigation licence is £2,500 per title for budgets under $500k, Windows only and without source; its Standard licence is £15,000 per title.

### Which UE5 3D navigation plugins support StateTree and Mass Entity?

LCM 3D Navigation AI ships 41 StateTree nodes and 13 Mass StateTree nodes with 8 Mass traits, for crowds of 10,000+ agents. AeonixNavigation includes a StateTree Move To task. None of the other options we checked document Mass Entity support.

### Do I need a bounds volume for 3D navigation in Unreal Engine 5?

With Mercuna, Flying Navigation System, AeonixNavigation and Nav3D, yes: each asks for a bounds or octree volume around the navigable space. LCM 3D Navigation AI's infinite mode needs none: navigation chunks stream in around the agents and unload behind them, so an open world has no edge to outgrow.

### Does DoN's 3D Pathfinding work in Unreal Engine 5?

DoN's 3D Pathfinding (DonAINavigation) was built for Unreal Engine 4; its last substantive update targets UE 4.19 (2018). LCM 3D Navigation AI supports Unreal Engine 5.2 to 5.8 and was last updated in October 2026.

### Is HyperNav available for Unreal Engine?

No. HyperNav 3D Pathfinding and Navigation is a Unity asset. For Unreal Engine 5, LCM 3D Navigation AI provides volumetric 3D navigation and pathfinding for flying, swimming and space AI.

Title: Flying AI & Drone AI for UE5 | LCM 3D Navigation AI
Description: Flying AI and drone AI for Unreal Engine 5: true 3D routes, 6-DOF flight, landing on moving decks, perching birds and combat drones that hunt and engage.

UEDEV / 3D Navigation AI / Flying AI · Updated 24 October 2026

**v3.6.0** Use case · Flying AI

# Flying AI and drones for Unreal Engine 5

Drones that bank into their turns, land on a rolling ship's deck and hunt through city streets, and birds that glide in to perch on a cliff ledge. LCM 3D Navigation AI gives every flying agent a real route through the air, a 6-DOF body that flies it, and a library of ready-made behaviours, from one hero drone to a Mass Entity flock.
[★★★★★Rated 5.0 out of 5 from3 ratings on Fab↗](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73?tab=reviews)

[Get it on Fab](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73)
See the demo levels
How it works

- LCM 3D Navigation AI

- Unreal Engine 5.2–5.8

- 4: Flight archetypes

- 85: BT, StateTree & Mass nodes

- 10,000+: Mass Entity agents

- 5.2–5.8: Unreal Engine

_Drones and their planned routes over a streamed city_

01 · Routes

## A route through the air, not along a floor

Unreal's Recast navmesh describes where a character can stand. A drone needs to know where there is empty air, so LCM 3D Navigation AI carves the level into a Sparse Voxel Octree of navigable volume and plans through it in full 3D: up, down and diagonally through shafts, under bridges and between towers.

Theta* and Lazy Theta* give any-angle routes that cut the corners a grid would force, and every smoothed path is checked against the level's geometry, so a drone never cuts through a wall to reach its goal.

_A multirotor drone over the harbour quay_

02 · Flight

## A body that flies like the real thing

Navigation gives guidance; `LcmFlightMovementComponent` turns it into flight. Four archetypes each bank, climb, glide and stop differently: **Multirotor drone** (tilt-to-translate), **Jet / Fixed-Wing**, **Bird** (flap-glide) and **Fish**. Thrust, lift, drag and an attitude PID drive the body, with inertia, turn-rate limits and arrival deceleration, and an animation-drive struct feeds your blendspaces.

Flight follows the level's gravity (World Settings or a Physics Volume), and Max Pitch, Flare Pitch and Leg Friction are set per bird in its Flight Config.

_Gulls sweep in and one settles on the sea stack_

03 · Take off, land, perch

## Landing, even on a moving deck

The **Land** task finds its own landing point and flies the approach relative to the deck, so a courier drone can put down on a moving, rolling ship or a moving lorry and take off again with the deck's velocity. Drones descend vertically; birds glide in with a braking flare. EQS generators and tests find landing sites for flying agents.

**Perch** lands on tagged ledges and pads, and agents in a crowd share the work: no two take the same perch. Since 3.6 drones no longer bob over a perch or a landing pad, and gliding birds land from where they are.

_Hunter drones weave between container stacks_

04 · Combat AI

## Drones that hunt, engage and search

**Engage Target** finds a firing position, keeps line of sight and fires only on a clean shot. In 3.6 it holds that position until the target leaves it, flies to it in formation and leads a crossing target. **Investigate** searches around a last-known position, hunters remember what they lose sight of, **Flee** breaks line of sight and hides, and **Scan Area** sweeps a volume.

Sentries can see only through Unreal's AI Perception sight cones, and Engage can take its sightings from AI Perception.

_The Fly To Location node in the Feature Examples hall_

05 · Authoring

## Behaviour Tree, StateTree or one Blueprint node

Author the same flight in the system your team already uses: 21 Behaviour Tree tasks, 5 decorators and 5 services; 25 StateTree tasks, 8 conditions and 8 evaluators at full parity; or Mass StateTree for crowds. For the simplest case, the `Fly To Location` latent node flies any pawn to a point or an actor with no Behaviour Tree, StateTree or AI Controller, and Unreal's own Move To and EQS can plan through the octree too.

Free demo levels

These levels are part of the 57 free demo levels you download from inside the editor (LCM Nav3D menu › Get the Demo Levels).

### Harbour

### Hunter Drone

FAQ

## Common questions

### How do I make a drone fly to a location in Unreal Engine 5?

Place one LcmNavigationManagerSVO in the level so it builds the navigation octree, add LcmFlightMovementComponent to the drone pawn with the Multirotor archetype, then use the Fly To task in a Behaviour Tree or StateTree. For a one-off move, the Fly To Location Blueprint node flies the pawn with no AI Controller at all.

### Can a drone land on a moving ship or vehicle?

Yes. The Land task finds its own landing point and flies the approach relative to the deck, so a drone can land on a moving, rolling ship or a moving lorry and take off again with the deck's velocity. The Harbour demo shows both.

### Which flight models are included?

Four 6-DOF archetypes: Multirotor drone (tilt-to-translate), Jet / Fixed-Wing, Bird (flap-glide) and Fish (undulatory), each with its own banking, climb and turn character and tuned per agent.

### Can flying AI and ground AI share a level?

Yes. Run hybrid levels where walking agents use Unreal's Recast navmesh and flying agents use the volumetric octree; the Crowd Avoidance Bridge lets Detour steer Recast agents around flying pawns.

### Why doesn't AI Move To work for flying AI in Unreal Engine 5?

AI Move To follows Unreal's Recast navmesh, which only describes walkable floors, so it has no route through the air. LCM 3D Navigation AI adds a volumetric octree of the empty space with its own Fly To task and Fly To Location node, so a pawn moves to any point in 3D, over, under and between obstacles, with no floor needed.

### How do I make a flying enemy that chases the player?

Use the Follow Target or Engage Target task in a Behaviour Tree or StateTree. The drone plans a 3D route to the player and re-plans as they move, and the 3D EQS tests pick positions with a clear line of sight. The Hunter Drone demo shows one hunting a target through container stacks.

Read more in the free documentation:

- [Your first flying agent ↗](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/your-first-flying-agent.html)

- [Flight and locomotion ↗](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/flight-locomotion.html)

- [Fly To Location node ↗](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/fly-to-location.html)

- [AI perception ↗](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/ai-perception.html)

- [Tactical EQS ↗](https://lcmnav3d.github.io/tactical-eqs.html)

[★★★★★Rated 5.0 out of 5 from3 ratings on Fab↗](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73?tab=reviews)

How it works

- LCM 3D Navigation AI

- Unreal Engine 5.2–5.8

- 0.5cm: Smallest voxel

- 1cm: Fish Tank demo voxels

_Fish over the coral in the Coral Reef demo_

01 · Volume

## The whole water column

A navmesh with a depth offset is a floor plan. LCM 3D Navigation AI routes swimming agents through the full volume (over reefs, under structures and through arches) on genuine 3D paths. Fish inside a Water Volume never swim out of it, and since 3.6 water volumes and overlap-only triggers no longer read as solid to the agents' own checks, so fish find cover and turtles find the seabed.

_Angelfish above the reef_

02 · New in 3.6

## Fish that swim like fish

Fish keep their depth by pointing the nose instead of sliding up and down, swim upright, school side by side and in layers, and turn away from walls at once. The tail beats with the swimming speed (Tail Beat From Speed in the Flight Config) and a skeletal fish's swim animation plays at the same rate.

A fish slows down so its turning circle fits the way onto its target instead of circling it, and keeps its personal space even with schooling off. Its body size is measured from its meshes.

_A Mass school turning together over the reef_

03 · Schooling

## Schooling, for one pawn or a Mass crowd

Turn on Schooling on a Mass crowd or on a pawn's Flight Movement component and it steers as a school: personal space, collision anticipation, heading matching, and turning away from rocks and glass before reaching them. A few informed fish lead the rest, a predator sets off a fountain escape that spreads through the school, and fish swim in bursts and glides. Distances are in body lengths, so it works at any scale.

_The 1 cm fish tank, captured in real time_

04 · Small worlds

## An aquarium at 1 cm

Voxels go down to 0.5 cm, and a World Scale profile handles centimetre-scale worlds. The Fish Tank demo navigates a 120 cm aquarium at 1 cm: 8 cm fish through a rock arch and round a predator's lair, in Behaviour Tree, StateTree and Mass editions.

_8 cm fish at small-world scale_

05 · Behaviours

## Behaviours under water

The same behaviour library works for swimmers. In the Coral Reef demo an ROV surveys the reef with **Scan Area**, the school darts into the coral out of its sight with **Flee**, groupers turn to watch it with **Look At**, and turtles settle on the seabed with **Perch**.

### How do I make fish AI swim in Unreal Engine 5?

### Do fish stay inside a Water Volume?

_A fleet through the Deep Space asteroid field_

01 · Free-floating

## Navigation with nothing to stand on

A surface navmesh has nothing to project onto in space. The octree treats a debris field, an asteroid belt or a station interior as ordinary navigable volume, so routes go over, under and between rocks in any direction. Flight takes its gravity from the level (World Settings or a Physics Volume) instead of a fixed value.

_A fighter leads its target between asteroids_

02 · Chase

## Chase, intercept, re-plan

In the Space Dogfight demo, Fly To in chase mode follows a target that breaks, jinks behind rocks and turns back for head-on passes, re-planning through the octree as it moves while both squads trade fire. _Pursuit past bright asteroids in a streamed level_

03 · Streaming

## A belt with no edge

The asteroid belt is an infinite world: navigation chunks stream in around the fighters and are discarded behind them, so memory stays flat however far the fight drifts. Long routes solve coarsely across chunks and finely within the current one.

_Starfighters trading laser fire_

The Raider Swarm demo runs a Mass swarm of eighteen raiders that sweeps the belt and closes round any fighter it sees, sharing the positions round it, while six fighters hunt them one by one with Fly To in chase mode. ## Common questions

### How do I make spaceship AI in Unreal Engine 5?

Place an LcmNavigationManagerSVO (in infinite mode for a large or unbounded space), give the ship LcmFlightMovementComponent with the Jet / Fixed-Wing archetype, and drive it with the Fly To task in a Behaviour Tree or StateTree; Fly To has a chase mode for moving targets.

### Does it need a floor or gravity?

No. The octree stores navigable volume in every direction, and flight takes its gravity from the level rather than a fixed value.

### Can it handle an asteroid field that streams in?

Yes. In infinite mode navigation chunks stream in around agents and unload behind them, and the Space Dogfight and Deep Space demos both run in streamed asteroid fields.

Title: Open-World 3D Navigation for UE5 | LCM 3D Navigation AI
Description: Open-world 3D navigation for Unreal Engine 5: chunks stream around your agents with no bounds volume, a long-range graph, pre-baked chunks and GPU builds.

UEDEV / 3D Navigation AI / Open worlds · Updated 24 October 2026

**v3.6.0** Use case · Open worlds

# Open-world 3D navigation for Unreal Engine 5

Most volumetric navigation starts by asking for a bounds volume, and navigation simply ends at its edge. Infinite mode removes the box: navigation streams in around your agents and is discarded behind them, so memory stays flat however far the map runs.
[★★★★★Rated 5.0 out of 5 from3 ratings on Fab↗](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73?tab=reviews)

[Get it on Fab](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73)
See the demo levels
How it works

- LCM 3D Navigation AI

- Unreal Engine 5.2–5.8

- 0: Bounds volumes needed

- GPU: Built chunk octrees

- 3: Streamed demo worlds

- 5.2–5.8: Unreal Engine

_The streamed octree and routes over the city, chunk by chunk_

01 · Streaming

## No bounds volume, no edge

A bounds volume has to contain everywhere an agent may ever fly, and memory scales with that box whether or not anything is happening inside it. In infinite mode, navigation chunks are generated around the agents as they travel and discarded behind them, for the same reason you stream level geometry rather than loading a continent.

For an arena or a level-sized map, finite mode builds once at `BeginPlay` or bakes to an asset, with the lowest overhead.

_Drones on long routes across the city_

02 · Long routes

## Planning beyond what has loaded

Long routes use macro/micro routing: the path solves coarsely across chunks and finely within the chunk the agent is in, so a cross-map flight never pays full-resolution search cost end to end. A persistent long-range graph keeps planning through geometry that has not streamed in yet.

`Find Path Detailed` tells a complete route from one that stops short of the goal in a streamed world, and the query option Require Complete Path makes a partial route fail instead.

_Routes over the forest canopy to the rocky massif_

03 · Bake or stream

## Pre-baked where you want it, streamed everywhere else

Bake the authored parts of a world ahead of time and stream the rest: streamed worlds can use pre-baked chunks, and navigation rebuilds automatically when levels stream in. Moving obstacles are cheap in streamed worlds too.

_Cost areas priced across streamed chunk seams_

04 · GPU-built

## Chunks built on the GPU, and checked

Each streamed chunk's voxels, octree and links are built on the GPU on D3D12, D3D11 and Vulkan. Each machine's GPU proves its voxels before it builds navigation, and the GPU build checks its own output word by word and rebuilds what it cannot repair. Cost areas (storms, no-fly zones, toll gates) are priced across chunk seams.

FAQ

## Common questions

### Does it work with World Partition and open worlds?

Yes. In infinite mode navigation chunks stream in around agents and unload behind them, so 3D pathfinding keeps working across an open-world or World Partition project rather than only inside a hand-placed box.

### What happens when a route reaches past the loaded area?

A persistent long-range graph keeps planning beyond loaded geometry, and Find Path Detailed reports whether a route is complete or stops short of the goal; Require Complete Path makes a partial route fail instead.

### Can I pre-bake parts of an open world?

Yes. Finite levels can be baked to an asset, and streamed worlds can use pre-baked chunks alongside chunks generated at runtime.

# Mass Entity flying crowds for Unreal Engine 5

Drone swarms, bird flocks and fish schools in true 3D through Unreal's Mass ECS: 10,000+ agents on per-agent paths or one shared flow field, with crowds that perch, scan, engage, investigate and flee.
[★★★★★Rated 5.0 out of 5 from3 ratings on Fab↗](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73?tab=reviews)

[Get it on Fab](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73)
See the demo levels
How it works

- LCM 3D Navigation AI

- Unreal Engine 5.2–5.8

- 10,000+: Mass Entity agents

- 8: Mass traits

- 13: Mass StateTree nodes

- O(1): Flow-field sampling

_One shared flow field carries the swarm over the skyline_

01 · Two modes

## Per-agent paths or one shared flow field

Crowds heading the same way sample one shared CPU flow field in constant time, while the agents that matter get their own asynchronous paths. Auto-registered processors handle request, solve and steer, so you never call the solver yourself. A crowd's first flow field is built off the game thread, so a crowd spawning into a streamed world does not cost one long frame.

_Close fly-through of the swarm_

02 · Behaviours

## Crowds that behave, not just move

Ten Mass StateTree tasks and three evaluators let crowds perch, scan, engage, investigate and flee. Agents in a crowd share the work: they sweep an area sharing the viewpoints, close round an intruder the moment any of them sees it, and no two take the same perch, cover or vantage point.

_A school turning together without overlapping_

03 · Density

## Dense crowds that do not overlap

Hold Avoidance Between Scans keeps separation on every frame, and Contact Push pushes apart bodies that overlap, including agents that have arrived, so a crowd no longer piles onto its goal. A crowd agent pushed off the flow field's covered space steers back instead of freezing, and schooling works for Mass crowds as well as pawns.

_A swarm climbing through a tower interior_

04 · Setup

## One trait, no code

Add a trait to a Mass Entity Config and the crowd navigates in full 3D, with no per-agent controller and no tick function. Eight traits cover movement, guidance, goals, perception, behaviour status and rendering, and an editor validator flags illegal combinations. The one rule: exactly one movement trait per agent. Crowds render through instanced meshes with LOD representation.

FAQ

## Common questions

### How many agents can navigate in 3D through Mass Entity?

10,000 or more. Crowds can use per-agent asynchronous paths or one shared flow field that the whole swarm samples in constant time, and they render through instanced meshes with LOD.

### Do I need C++ to use Mass crowds?

No. Add the traits to a Mass Entity Config; an editor validator flags illegal trait combinations, and Mass StateTree tasks drive the behaviour.

### Can crowds use behaviours like perch and engage?

Yes. Ten Mass StateTree tasks and three evaluators let crowds perch, scan, engage, investigate and flee, and agents share viewpoints, perches and cover so no two take the same one.

### Does it support 3D flow fields for crowds?

Yes. A Mass crowd can share one CPU flow field toward a goal, which every agent samples in constant time, or plan per-agent asynchronous paths; both work in full 3D, through the air or water.

Title: Moving Obstacle Avoidance for UE5 AI | LCM 3D Navigation AI

UEDEV / 3D Navigation AI / Moving obstacles · Updated 24 October 2026

**v3.6.0** Use case · New in 3.6

# Moving obstacle avoidance for Unreal Engine 5 AI

Re-planning around a door after it closes is too late for a drone at speed. Since 3.6, Fly To predicts where every moving obstacle will be and times its pass, and the octree still restamps itself as the world moves, so routes stay true.
[★★★★★Rated 5.0 out of 5 from3 ratings on Fab↗](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73?tab=reviews)

[Get it on Fab](https://www.fab.com/listings/92f05e42-d7be-4de3-abe8-7b0a3e70ba73)
See the demo levels
How it works

- LCM 3D Navigation AI

- Unreal Engine 5.2–5.8

- 42: Movers in the Gauntlet

- 370m: Gauntlet hall

- 200: Agent Mass edition

- 3: Prediction settings

_Same start, three departure times: each drone predicts the gate and takes the route that is fastest for its moment_

01 · Prediction

## Predict, don't just react

Fly To predicts where every moving obstacle (any actor with an LCM Dynamic Obstacle component) will be, and times its pass. It learns a gate's or a piston's cycle and replays it, turns a spinning blade with it, eases off, waits for a gap or takes a detour, and dodges what it cannot outrun.

It is on by default in the Behaviour Tree and StateTree Fly To, controlled by three settings: **Avoid Moving Obstacles**, **Moving Obstacle Look-Ahead** and **Moving Obstacle Margin**.

_Land on a moving platform in the Feature Examples hall_

02 · Live octree

## The octree moves with the world

Moving geometry writes its own footprint back into the octree as it travels, so doors, lifts, moving platforms, destructible cover and patrolling ships change routing live, and in multiplayer the change is multicast to every peer. A mover put back to the start of its track is treated as a jump, not a very fast move, so the space it left is freed.

In streamed worlds a moving obstacle's update next to a 168k-triangle room costs about 1 ms, down from 20 ms.

_Agents keeping apart in a dense swarm_

03 · Each other

## Avoiding each other, too

Agents avoid each other with Reactive (boids), Predictive (ORCA) or Context-Based Steering, chosen per agent. Fly To's wall-avoidance whiskers ignore other agents and leave them to agent avoidance, and Mass crowds keep apart with Hold Avoidance and Contact Push.

New demo · 3.6

## The Obstacle Gauntlet

A 370 m hall of six zones with 42 movers driven by Unreal's own movement components. Twelve drones fly it end to end in the Behaviour Tree and StateTree editions; a crowd of 200 follows a beacon through it in the Mass edition. Open it from the demo menu.

- **ZONE 01**Fast gates

- **ZONE 02**Crossing traffic

- **ZONE 03**Windmills and sweepers

- **ZONE 04**Pistons

- **ZONE 05**Head-on blocks

- **ZONE 06**Bouncers

FAQ

## Common questions

### How do AI agents avoid moving obstacles in Unreal Engine 5?

Give the moving actor an LCM Dynamic Obstacle component. Its footprint restamps the navigation octree as it moves, and since 3.6 the Fly To task predicts its motion and times its pass: waiting for a gap, taking a detour or dodging.

### Does it work with doors, lifts and moving platforms?

Yes. Any moving actor with a Dynamic Obstacle component updates the octree live, agents re-route around it, and the change replicates to clients in multiplayer.

### Which settings control moving-obstacle prediction?

Avoid Moving Obstacles turns it on (it is on by default), Moving Obstacle Look-Ahead sets how far ahead Fly To predicts, and Moving Obstacle Margin sets the clearance it keeps.

# Niagara VFX packs for Unreal Engine

## LCM 3D Navigation AI

True 3D pathfinding and volumetric navigation for Unreal Engine 5: flying, swimming and free-floating AI, 85 Behaviour Tree, StateTree and Mass nodes, 10,000+ agent crowds and infinite streaming worlds. ★★★★★ 5.0 on Fab.

## Capabilities

What UEDEV builds for Unreal teams, from navigation and AI down through the effects layer.

01

### Volumetric 3D Navigation

LCM 3D Navigation AI: sparse voxel octree pathfinding with GPU voxelization, Mass crowds and true-3D tactical queries for flying and swimming agents.

02

### Game AI

Behaviour trees, detour steering and decision systems that stay smooth as agent counts climb.

03

### Gameplay Systems

Combat, physics and runtime ECS architectures written in C++ for shipping-grade performance.

04

### Real-time VFX

Production-grade Niagara effects (explosions, beams, shields and environments), profiled to hold frame budget.

05

### Engine Tooling

Editor plugins and pipeline tools that take the repetitive work out of your team's day.

01 About Me

## Building worlds, one system at a time

I'm **L. Charitha Madhushanka**, a Senior Game Developer with an **MSc in Computer Games (Distinction)** from the University of Essex. For over six years I've shipped commercial games, VR/AR experiences and engine tools, currently as Senior Gameplay Engineer at **Ripstone Games** on an unannounced PlayStation title.

My focus is the craft behind play: combat and AI, physics-driven mechanics, crowd and pathfinding systems, runtime ECS and Niagara VFX. I also publish high-quality content to the Unreal marketplace: **11 products, 150+ assets** used by developers worldwide.

### Unreal Engine

4 commercially published games

- 4+ virtual reality applications

- 2+ augmented reality applications

- Marketplace asset publishing

### Unity Engine

- 2 commercially published games

- 5+ virtual reality applications

- 4+ augmented reality applications

- Interactive media & simulators

05 Devlog · Systems

## Game AI & 3D navigation systems

Engineering deep-dives into the systems I build in Unreal Engine: 3D navigation & pathfinding, crowd AI, runtime ECS and Niagara VFX. The code behind the games.

AI · Pathfinding
### Voxel 3D Pathfinding System

Full 3D navigation through voxelized space for flying & climbing agents.

AI · Crowds
### Detour Crowd Avoidance

Scalable crowd movement with smooth local avoidance between agents.

Architecture
### Runtime ECS Development

Data-oriented entity-component-system for high-performance gameplay.

VFX · Tech Art
### Advanced Niagara VFX

Marketplace-grade particle systems & effects authored in Niagara.

Combat
### Monsters Domain Combat Dev

Building the melee combat & enemy AI behaviours for the RPG.

## Play my Rubik's Cube Solver

A fully interactive 3D Rubik's cube: drag to rotate, scan a real cube with your camera, then follow a guided **7-phase solve** with live algorithm playback. A little side project that shows how I turn systems into playable, teachable tools.

3D engineCamera scanKociemba solverGuided tutorial
